UnitStatement: Chirality's epistemology has six primitives: claim, warrant, status, gap, conflict, and ruling.
The warrant lifecycle tracks the epistemic state of claims alongside the deliverable production lifecycle.
The epistemic architecture makes the epistemic status of every claim transparent and auditable.
The epistemic architecture supports professional reliance decisions without claiming to improve LLM output quality.
LLM output is optimized for plausibility rather than inherent factual warrant.
LLMs may produce fluent, specific, confident outputs that are incorrect, unsupported, or fabricated.
The term hallucination understates the architectural significance of LLM reliability failures.
A model output carries no intrinsic epistemic warrant.
Correct and incorrect LLM claims are generated by the same mechanism and can share the same surface properties.
Professional authentication of a PWP means accepting personal responsibility for accuracy, completeness, and fitness for purpose.
APEGA authentication requires direct supervision and control or a thorough review.
Professional review presupposes the ability to distinguish known, assumed, extracted, inferred, supported, and unsupported claims.
Uncontrolled LLM output lacks provenance, epistemic labels, and boundaries between knowledge and interpolation.
Without architectural controls, thorough review of LLM output becomes complete independent verification.
Chirality's epistemic architecture makes review targeted rather than exhaustive by exposing each claim's epistemic status.
K-PROV-1 requires every extracted dependency row to cite EvidenceFile and SourceRef or explicitly mark location TBD.
Every non-trivial claim in a governed workflow must include a source path and best-effort section reference or an explicit missing-source marker.
Dependencies.csv v3.1 defines EvidenceFile, SourceRef, and EvidenceQuote as required provenance columns.
EvidenceFile records the source document filename or location TBD.
SourceRef records the path and heading or section within the evidence file, or location TBD.
EvidenceQuote records a short supporting quote and is recommended to stay under 30 words.
Provenance columns are required schema fields, not optional metadata.
A dependency row without provenance is flagged as a quality finding.
The R5 workflow design requirement extends provenance to all agent outputs through SourcePath and best-effort SectionRef.
A fully provenanced dependency row carries a specific source section, a direct quote, HIGH confidence, and EXPLICIT explicitness.
An inferred dependency row can identify a source file while marking the supporting section as location TBD.
An inferred dependency row can carry MEDIUM confidence, IMPLICIT explicitness, and an ASSUMPTION note.
Epistemic differences between claims must be visible in the data rather than hidden in model reasoning.
K-INVENT-1 requires unknown values to become TBD rather than guessed.
Agents must not invent scope items, dependency targets, parameter values, or engineering content.
Agent instruction invariants enforce the no-invention rule across agents.
Type 2 agents halt with FAILED_INPUTS when required inputs are invalid.
Type 2 agents continue with TBD markings and warnings when optional data is missing.
The dangerous LLM failure mode is plausible-looking output for quantities that are actually unknown.
No-invention represents absent data as absent data rather than as a confident-looking fabrication.
When design pressure is missing from a vendor datasheet, K-INVENT-1 requires Design Pressure to be marked TBD with a clarification note.
K-CONFLICT-1 requires conflicts between sources to be surfaced rather than silently resolved.
Agents must expose source disagreements with pointers to the conflicting sources.
When conflicting information is encountered, the agent produces a Conflict Table.
A Conflict Table includes ConflictID, Key, Contenders, ProposedAuthority, and HumanRuling fields.
ProposedAuthority may suggest a governing source only as a PROPOSAL.
HumanRuling remains TBD until a licensed professional adjudicates the conflict.
Agents never silently pick a winner between conflicting sources.
LLMs may obscure source disagreements by choosing one value, averaging values, or synthesizing the conflict away.
Regulated practice requires source conflicts to reach the decision-maker for documented, traceable, defensible professional judgment.
Conflict visibility is architecturally enforced so disagreements are not hidden from engineering review.
Every non-trivial claim produced by an agent is classified with an epistemic label.
FACT means a claim is directly observed in source text with citation.
ASSUMPTION means a reasonable inference is not directly stated and requires validation.
PROPOSAL means an agent suggestion requires a human decision before it becomes binding.
TBD means an unknown placeholder requires resolution before reliance.
Epistemic labels are defined in TYPES.md Section 10 and required by agent instruction invariants.
Epistemic labeling turns review into triage over FACTs, ASSUMPTIONs, PROPOSALs, and TBDs.
With epistemic labeling, review effort becomes proportional to actual uncertainty rather than output volume.
The four epistemic mechanisms form a coherent epistemic theory rather than independent quality rules.
Provenance answers where a claim comes from.
No invention answers what happens when the answer is unknown.
Conflict surfacing answers what happens when sources disagree.
Epistemic labeling answers how certain a claim is.
The provenance requirement makes ungrounded claims visible.
TBD marking makes fabricated values for unknown quantities visible.
Conflict Tables make source disagreements visible.
Epistemic labels make ambiguous certainty status visible.
The common thread across the mechanisms is visibility of epistemic failure to the reviewer.
Chirality does not guarantee prevention of epistemic failures; it makes failures structurally detectable.
The architecture treats guaranteed prevention of LLM epistemic failures as impossible, while detection can be enforced.
The warrant lifecycle is the epistemic counterpart to the deliverable production lifecycle.
The deliverable lifecycle tracks production stage but not the epistemic state of claims within a deliverable.
A deliverable in IN_PROGRESS may contain claims with multiple warrant states.
The warrant lifecycle states are UNWARRANTED, CITED, REVIEWED, and AUTHENTICATED.
Each claim occupies a warrant lifecycle position independently of the deliverable production state.
The aggregate warrant state of a deliverable determines readiness for the next production transition.
A newly produced agent claim is initially UNWARRANTED until extrinsic justification is attached.
Under K-PROV-1, the agent's epistemic task is to attach a warrant consisting of source file, section reference, and ideally supporting quote.
If an agent cannot find a warrant, K-INVENT-1 requires the claim to be marked TBD as an explicit gap.
The UNWARRANTED to CITED transition is the agent's primary epistemic contribution.
A CITED claim has provenance but is not yet sufficient for professional reliance.
Professional review of a CITED claim assesses source authority, citation accuracy, and interpretation reasonableness.
The REVIEW agent's 5-gate protocol structures the assessment of cited claims.
A claim transitions from CITED to REVIEWED after the professional examines it and dispositions findings.
Authentication declares that the deliverable's aggregate warrant state is sufficient for reliance under professional responsibility.
The REVIEWED to AUTHENTICATED transition applies to the deliverable as a whole rather than individual claims.
Authentication binds to a specific git SHA under K-AUTH-2 so the warrant-to-content relationship is mechanically verifiable.
Thorough review is operationally the process of auditing warrant sufficiency.
Professional review includes examining claims, checking warrants, resolving gaps and conflicts through rulings, and deciding whether aggregate warrant state supports authentication.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC classifies every non-trivial claim in a deliverable's document kit by warrant state.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC reports epistemic label coverage, provenance completeness rates, potential conflicts, and a warrant state summary.
AUDIT_EPISTEMIC makes the warrant lifecycle auditable and measurable for every deliverable.
The epistemic architecture is complementary to model-level improvements.
RLHF improves average model output quality by training toward outputs human raters prefer.
RLHF does not provide per-claim epistemic status.
RLHF is a population-level improvement, while the epistemic architecture is per-claim annotation.
RAG grounds model output by retrieving relevant documents and presenting them with the prompt.
RAG is insufficient because the model may interpolate beyond retrieved content without marking the boundary.
The epistemic architecture requires every claim to carry provenance to a specific source.
Claims that go beyond source content must carry ASSUMPTION or PROPOSAL labels.
Post-hoc factuality checking verifies model outputs against a reference corpus after generation.
Post-hoc factuality checking introduces checker reliability questions and does not provide per-claim epistemic labels.
The epistemic architecture produces per-claim labels during generation rather than as a post-hoc audit.
Constitutional AI trains models to self-critique against principles.
Constitutional AI does not provide extrinsic provenance.
The epistemic architecture requires specific file paths and section references rather than model self-assessment.
Chirality's contribution is a governance architecture that makes model epistemic limitations visible and manageable.
Better models reduce the number of TBD and ASSUMPTION labels, while the architecture keeps remaining uncertainty visible.
The epistemic architecture makes the Chapter 6 regulatory mapping possible.
Thorough review requires the licensed professional to confirm reliability, accuracy, and validity of the work.
With epistemic labeling and provenance, reviewers can target effort to FACT citations, ASSUMPTION validation, PROPOSAL decisions, and TBD resolution.
Epistemic architecture makes review proportional to actual uncertainty rather than output volume.
Direct supervision and control requires periodic reviews to ensure PWPs are accurate and reliable.
Epistemic labels and provenance fields make periodic reviews efficient and targeted.
Targeted supervision checks the evidence trail, reviews flagged uncertainties, and adjudicates conflicts.
Authentication requires supervised or thoroughly reviewed work plus acceptance of professional responsibility.
The epistemic architecture provides provenance trails, labels, and conflict resolutions as the evidentiary basis for authentication.
Authentication is supported by a traceable record rather than by trust in the tool.
Chirality addresses absence of intrinsic epistemic warrant with mandatory provenance, no invention, conflict surfacing, and epistemic labeling.
The epistemic architecture transforms professional review from exhaustive verification to targeted assessment.
Most LLM reliability work focuses on reducing error rates, while Chirality focuses on transparent per-claim epistemic status.
Per-claim epistemic transparency is necessary for professional practice regardless of model quality.
The epistemic architecture makes Chapter 6 regulatory obligations tractable for AI-assisted work.
Chirality's structured evidence trail is more complete and auditable than manual practice typically achieves.
